# Brice Rigourd — Energy engineer and Python developer

> Energy engineer (solar PV, wind, grid connection) who builds the Python tools that replace manual work for technical teams.

Last updated: October 2026 · Version française: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/llms-full.txt · Portfolio: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/

- Target roles: Renewable energy study engineer (solar PV, wind) ; Grid connection engineer ; PV performance and operations engineer ; Python developer: data, automation, business tools ; Hybrid role combining energy and Python or AI development

## Summary

ESTIA engineer with a Master's in Smart Grids from the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU). I write the software that replaces manual work for technical teams: tools that read thousands of PDFs, desktop applications, Excel/VBA tools and AI prototypes. I have delivered tools to Amarenco (solar power producer), to Energiter (wind and solar engineering consultancy) and for a medical-device manufacturer.

## Key figures

- 287 PV plants in operation under my supervision at the end of the assignment (14 SPVs, 67.3 MWp, mostly rooftop).
- Over 230 PVsyst studies with discrepancies against the monitoring configuration identified and reported, over a hundred of them being redone.
- Technical database updates and checks against SharePoint cut from 2 to 3 weeks to under 10 minutes.
- 4,128 PVsyst reports retrieved and analyzed automatically; 2,150 grid access contracts read and checked.
- Over 40 PV feasibility and yield studies, over 15 wind simulations.
- Over 3,400 French source substations filtered and ranked in 5 to 20 seconds.
- About 18,000 lines of Python in the Amarenco tools; about 4,750 lines of VBA in PlasmaCraft.

## Professional experience

### Consulting engineer, PV operations — Amarenco (Toulouse, France)

January 2025 – December 2025 · Solar power producer

Operations of a portfolio of 287 PV plants at the end of the assignment (14 SPVs, 67.3 MWp, mostly rooftop) and development of the team's automation tools.

- Plant performance monitoring (performance ratio, expected yield) in the 3E SynaptiQ monitoring platform.
- Monthly reports to shareholders, KPI and OPEX budget tracking, Asset Management and O&M contracts.
- About 18,000 lines of Python in the final versions of the team's tools; typed package (mypy --strict, ruff, black, pytest).
- Feedback from a user about the automated analysis of maintenance reports (translated from French): "an absolutely brilliant tool".

#### Project: PVsyst ↔ SynaptiQ quality control (March – June 2025)

Check PVsyst studies against each plant's digital twin in SynaptiQ to explain inconsistent performance ratios: misconfigured twin, wrong PVsyst simulation, or both.

- About 154,000 SharePoint documents inventoried across 4,660 projects; about 7,500 PVsyst files kept (latest version of each project).
- Full extraction of the SynaptiQ API: 970 active plants, 1,794 module groups, 4,383 inverters.
- Automated comparison: tilt/azimuth pairs (identical, within ±1° or ±10°), module count per pair and five losses; matching by project code or by name.
- Over 230 PVsyst studies with discrepancies reported to the teams, over a hundred being redone; mostly orientation discrepancies (azimuth in the wrong cardinal direction) and module counts per orientation.

Technologies: Python, asyncio, SynaptiQ REST API (JWT), SharePoint, MSAL, requests, pandas, openpyxl, pdfplumber, pypdf, regex, fuzzywuzzy

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/controle-qualite.html

#### Project: PVsyst orchestrator (July – September 2025)

My first Python application with a graphical interface, built to keep the internal technical database up to date with the new PVsyst studies uploaded to SharePoint every week by internal and external design offices.

- Read-only SharePoint connection; the latest PVsyst studies of each SPV are located and downloaded into a local database, with an archive of older versions.
- Multiprocess extraction of PVsyst v6 to v8 reports, in French and English, then comparison with the internal technical database: missing or outdated data, by SPV and project code.
- Project status checks (cancelled, renamed, merged SPVs) and three Excel control workbooks to verify the tool's work.
- Full update in 1 to 10 minutes instead of 2 to 3 weeks by hand; simple check in 10 seconds to 5 minutes; first download of a portfolio of more than 300 plants in 30 minutes to 1 h 20.
- Validated and used from time to time by 3 fellow engineers, then handed by the department to a development team for internal deployment.
- Batch analyses: 26,809 DC/AC ratios extracted and 2,051 plants sorted into six clipping-risk classes; 2,150 grid access contracts read.

Technologies: Python, PySide6, QML, PyInstaller, concurrent.futures, requests, MSAL, pandas, openpyxl, pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, regex, mypy, pytest

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/amarenco.html

### Renewable energy design engineer (final-year internship) — Energiter (Montpellier, France)

April 2024 – September 2024 · Wind and solar engineering consultancy

Wind and solar feasibility studies, yield referent, and development of a grid connection study tool.

- Over 40 PV feasibility and yield studies: MV-connected plants from 2 to 22 MWp, PVsyst with Solargis data.
- Over 15 wind simulations in WAsP and windPRO: 3 to 15 MW wind farms, ERA5 and MERRA data.
- Grid connection studies for RTE and Enedis source substations.
- Bat-curtailment method in windPRO, validated against the in-house Python tool (about one point of difference on two wind farms).

#### Project: Grid connection study tool (Master's thesis subject) (April – September 2024)

Find the best source substation to connect a wind or solar farm, from public grid data.

- Over 3,400 source substations filtered by downstream voltage (20 kV or more) and ranked by a 0-to-5 criticality score, in 5 to 20 seconds.
- Real road distance through the IGN routing API called asynchronously: about 64% less response time.
- Caparéseau (RTE) capacities and S3REnR regional schemes downloaded and archived; analysis with and without reinforcement works; costing in 17 MW modules, cable choice, network cost and regional cost share.
- Deliverables: KML for Google Earth, folium maps, a project database and a PDF report; Excel/VBA interface driving the Python scripts through PowerShell.

Technologies: Python, asyncio, IGN routing API, folium, KML, geopy, Dijkstra, Excel, VBA, PowerShell

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/energiter.html

### VBA designer-developer (second-year engineering internship) — Ezio Industrial Consulting (Biarritz, France)

May 2023 – August 2023 · Industrial consulting

Assignment for a medical-device manufacturer (cold-plasma sterilization): design and delivery of a complete application, from requirements to user manual.

- Training documents on machine capability, qualifications and ISO 13485.

#### Project: PlasmaCraft, recipe-authoring software (May – August 2023)

Excel/VBA software for authoring the machine's PLC recipes, designed from scratch.

- 53 VBA modules, about 4,750 lines, 115 procedures.
- Recipes of up to 100 sequences with four parameters controlled over time; input checks against the machine's limits and step size (0 to 3,600 s per sequence, 0 to 500 W, 0 to 5 sccm, 0 to 22 G).
- Ramps split into 5 to 25 steps that add up exactly; batch editing; TXT export for the PLC and locked XLSM recipes.
- All nine client requirements covered; a 33-page user manual and an installation guide; name and logo designed and approved by the client.

Technologies: Excel, VBA, UserForms, Balsamiq

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/plasmacraft.html

## Personal projects (Lab)

### Combat agent trained in simulation (test bed: AION 2) (October 2026, in progress)

An agent that reads the game screen and decides every action, trained first by imitation, then in a simulated arena.

- 640×360 capture at 7 frames per second, detection in about 3 ms without a GPU.
- Imitation learning on 1,864 examples: 39.4% accuracy against 21.6% for the majority class.
- 2.5D arena calibrated on the real game; 32 settings trained with the cross-entropy method, validation score from 16.9 to 19.2 out of 20.
- PySide6 Windows application, about 29,000 lines of Python and 740 pytest tests; external approach only, simulation mode by default.

Technologies: Python, PySide6, computer vision, imitation learning, cross-entropy method, pytest

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/labo-aion.html

### Pulse, a dating app (Since January 2026, in progress)

Full-stack Android app, from prototype to release 1.014.

- Expo SDK 54, React Native 0.81 and TypeScript; FastAPI and WebSocket server; Supabase database migrated from MongoDB.
- Photos on S3 storage through presigned URLs, with a hand-written SigV4 signature.
- About 70 API routes, 16,800 lines of TypeScript and 5,400 lines of server code, 135 commits.
- Developed with Claude and Claude Code after a prototype built with the Emergent agent.

Technologies: TypeScript, React Native, Expo, FastAPI, WebSocket, Supabase, S3

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/labo-pulse.html

### Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W as a USB mouse and keyboard (October 2026, completed)

A microcontroller that poses as a USB mouse and keyboard and draws in Paint, driven by a Python script.

- CircuitPython and USB HID; commands received over a serial port.
- Closed-loop control from the cursor's real position; Paint buttons located through UI Automation.
- About 680 lines of Python.

Technologies: CircuitPython, Python, USB HID, UI Automation

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/labo-pico.html

### KidsVid, AI-generated videos for children, made locally (September 2026, abandoned)

A 100% local, open-source pipeline producing narrated stories and nursery rhymes, in French and English.

- n8n orchestrates a FastAPI service chaining Ollama and Qwen3, Piper, SDXL through ComfyUI, ACE-Step and FFmpeg.
- About 2,100 lines of Python, 19 API routes, 3 n8n workflows.
- Lessons: licenses compatible with commercial use, YouTube's "inauthentic content" policy, COPPA obligations.

Technologies: Python, FastAPI, n8n, Ollama, ComfyUI, SDXL, FFmpeg

Detailed page: https://bricerigourd.github.io/Portfolio-Rigourd-Brice/en/labo-kidsvid.html
